description: Per-translation glossary overlay for the Wheel of Heaven Translation of The Gospel According to Luke (canon-cited chapters). Greek source convention overlay; may be promoted to central when subsequent NT compositions arrive and acquire cross-corpus reach.

entries.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται (Lk 21:32; cf. Mk 13:30 // Mt 24:34)
entries.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti ou mē parelthē hē genea hautē heōs an panta genētai
entries.partOfSpeech: Overlay rendering convention for Lk 21:32 *genea hautē* 'this generation' eschatological-imminence saying
entries.literal: truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things take place
entries.standardEnglish: this generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled (KJV/ASV); truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have happened (NIV)
entries.wohChoice: ASV/RSV-baseline 'this generation shall not pass away till all these things take place' surface rendering preserved; the five-reading-strata of *genea hautē* — (i) the literal-imminent reading (this 30-40-year generation, fully-fulfilled by 70 CE temple-destruction); (ii) the generation-of-the-end reading (whichever generation sees the signs); (iii) the Jewish-people reading (the Jewish nation as a race / lineage); (iv) the human-race-broadly reading; (v) the type-of-people reading (this kind of unbelieving generation) — all preserved in this overlay apparatus per Marcus 2009 + Nolland 1993 + Fitzmyer 1985.
entries.rationale: **Lk 21:32 *genea hautē* is the single most-eschatologically-contested saying of the Synoptic Olivet Discourse** and is one of the most-influential verses in early-Christian and modern-Christian eschatology. The Synoptic-parallel Mark 13:30 and Mt 24:34 deploy the identical formula. Greek *genea* (G1074) covers a semantic-breadth from 'generation' (the standard 30-40-year-cohort sense) to 'race' / 'nation' / 'type-of-people'. The five-reading-strata are documented in detail in Marcus AB Mark 9:30 // 13:30; Nolland WBC Luke on 21:32; Fitzmyer AB Luke X-XXIV on 21:32; Bovon Hermeneia Luke 3 on 21:32; France NIGTC Mark on 13:30. The eschatological-imminence problem (the apparent prediction that the generation hearing Jesus would see the end-of-the-age, which did not visibly come to pass in the 1st-c.) is one of the most-discussed NT-eschatology cruxes. The WoH-Translation surface rendering preserves the conventional translation and documents the five-reading-strata without adjudicating.
